Polarization filtering is achieved by creating cross-polarization between the emitted single photons and the pump laser via a zero-order quarter-wave plate, followed by a polarizing beam splitter and linear polarizer [Fig. 2(b)].32 While this cross-polarization scheme effectively removes pump light for self-assembled QDs, it alone does not suffice for nanowire QDs, as the irregular surface and multiple facets on the nanowire distort the polarization of the scattered light.20 To address this, we implement spatial filtering by coupling the emission into a single-mode fiber [Fig. 2(c)], which transmits the Gaussian dot emission while rejecting the flower-shaped scattered pump light [Fig. 2(d)].20 This hybrid approach achieves over 80 dB suppression of the excitation laser. The filtered QD signal is then sent either to a spectrometer for photoluminescence or to SNSPDs for time-resolved correlation measurements. A more detailed description of the experimental setup is presented in the supplementary material. After an initial photoluminescence survey, we identified a number of nanowire quantum dots that could be driven in pulsed resonant fluorescence without any additional processing; the device presented is representative of this subset.

The supplementary material provides the additional details on the experimental setups and measurement procedures.
